slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
When people think of Chenin Blanc, they often immediately picture the sweet Layon or the multi-sweetness Vouvray. But Chenin's true stage for demonstrating "remarkable aging potential" is actually the bone-dry Anjou Blanc and Saumur Blanc. These two AOCs are the classic entry point for Chenin Blanc dry whites, and the best starting place for appreciating this grape.

Course Learning Objectives

🍇 Chenin Blanc Varietal Character

Master Chenin's acidity, phenolic compounds, aromatic profile, and ripeness differences

🪨 Anjou Noir vs Saumur Blanc

Distinguish between the entirely different terroir logics of black schist and white tuffeau

🛢️ Vinification Choices

The impact of stainless steel vs. large old oak barrels vs. amphora

🌟 Leading Estates

Learn about representative producers such as Domaine des Roches Neuves, Domaine du Closel, and Nicolas Joly
slides.2.title: Anjou Blanc & Saumur Blanc — Two Terroir Philosophies
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Anjou Noir
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Black Anjou — dominated by Brioverian schist, dark soils with intense mineral tension
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Saumur Blanc Terroir
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Tuffeau tuffstone dominates, similar to Vouvray — chalky minerality, elegant balance
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Same Grape, Different Character
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Anjou Blanc is more expressive; Saumur Blanc is more restrained and elegant
slides.2.content:
Although Anjou Blanc and Saumur Blanc are geographically adjacent and both use Chenin Blanc, the dramatic difference in soils — black schist vs. white tuffeau — gives them completely different personalities. This is why the middle Loire is called the "Chenin Terroir Museum."

🌑 Anjou Blanc

  • Location: Anjou Noir (Black Anjou), southwest Maine-et-Loire
  • Soils: Brioverian schist (Late Precambrian, blue-black) + some volcanic rock
  • Area: ~1,000 ha
  • Regulations: ≥80% Chenin Blanc; up to 20% Sauvignon Blanc/Chardonnay permitted
  • Style: Expressive, deep mineral, flint + graphite aromas, firm body
  • Aging: Top wines 5–10 years

⚪ Saumur Blanc

  • Location: Around Saumur, confluence of Loire and Thouet rivers
  • Soils: Tuffeau tuffstone (Late Cretaceous) dominant, some limestone
  • Area: ~800 ha
  • Regulations: ≥80% Chenin Blanc; up to 20% Sauvignon Blanc/Chardonnay permitted
  • Style: Chalky minerality, white flowers, green apple, lemon zest, elegant balance
  • Aging: Top wines 5–8 years

🔍 One-line distinction:

Anjou Blanc is like Chenin's "trail runner" — powerful, deep mineral, a touch wild.
Saumur Blanc is like Chenin's "ballet dancer" — elegant, light, with fine chalky minerality.
slides.2.quiz.question: What is the most critical terroir difference between Anjou Blanc and Saumur Blanc?
slides.2.quiz.options.1: Soil — Anjou dominated by schist, Saumur by Tuffeau tuffstone
slides.2.quiz.explanation: Both AOCs require ≥80% Chenin Blanc, and their climates and regulations are similar. The most critical difference is the soil: Anjou Noir's Brioverian schist (Precambrian, blue-black) vs. Saumur's Tuffeau tuffstone (Cretaceous, white and porous). This geological divide gives the two sides completely different mineral textures: the schist's "graphite/flint" vs. the tuffstone's "chalk/wet stone."
slides.3.title: Savennières — The Pinnacle of Anjou Dry Whites
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Top Sub-Appellation
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Located within Anjou, produces only dry Chenin Blanc white wine
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Volcanic Terroir
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Rare in Anjou — volcanic rock mixed with schist, imparting unique tropical mineral tension
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Two Independent Crus
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Coulée de Serrant (7 ha, single-owner monopole) and La Roche-aux-Moines
slides.3.content:
Savennières is the top sub-AOC within Anjou Blanc, independent from the main AOC hierarchy, and regarded as the world benchmark for dry Chenin Blanc. Its exceptional geology — volcanic rock + schist + sand — allows Chenin to display extraordinary mineral depth and aging potential (top wines can age 30+ years).

📐 Savennières Regulations

  • Area: ~145 ha
  • Variety: 100% Chenin Blanc
  • Sweetness: Sec only (<8 g/L) — the only top Chenin AOC in Loire that prohibits sweet wines
  • Yield limit: 50 hL/ha (stricter than Anjou Blanc's 60 hL/ha)
  • Harvest: Must be by hand; multiple passes permitted

🌟 Two Independent Cru AOCs

  • Coulée de Serrant: 7 ha, owned exclusively by the Joly family (Domaine de la Coulée de Serrant) since 1130 AD. Joly is a global pioneer of biodynamic viticulture; the wines are considered a spiritual origin point of the natural wine movement
  • La Roche-aux-Moines: 33 ha, shared by several estates. Key producers: Domaine aux Moines, Château de Chamboureau

🍷 Style Profile

Young: green apple, quince, chamomile, white flowers, flint minerality → with grippy acidity and phenolic quality (Chenin's characteristic slight bitterness/astringency, like grapefruit pith).

With age: beeswax, roasted hazelnuts, Madeira-like oxidative notes, curry, dry hay — 10–30 year aging potential, the highest of any Loire dry white.
slides.4.title: Impact of Vinification on Chenin Dry Whites
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Stainless Steel Tank
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Preserves pure fruit aromas and mineral tension; mainstream for entry-level wines
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Old Oak Barrels
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Favored by top estates — imparts no obvious oak flavor, but adds textural depth
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Amphora / Concrete Egg
slides.4.highlights.2.content: New trend — retains mineral purity while adding complexity
slides.4.content:
Chenin Blanc responds to oak very differently from Chardonnay — it dislikes the "vanilla + butter" notes of new barrels, and pairs better with "neutral vessels." This is why Loire Chenin dry whites typically use large old oak barrels (500–600 L Demi-Muid) rather than standard 225 L barriques.

🥶 Stainless Steel Tank (Cuve Inox)

  • Properties: Precise temperature control, no oxidation, no flavor addition
  • Preserves: Fresh fruit aromas, mineral texture, pure acidity
  • Best for: Entry-level Anjou Blanc, Saumur Blanc, Vouvray Sec
  • Drawback: Lacks textural depth; limited aging potential

🛢️ Large Old Oak Barrel (Demi-Muid 500–600 L)

  • Properties: Large capacity, slow oak release, gentle micro-oxygenation
  • Effect: Adds no obvious oak flavor, but makes the wine rounder and more structured
  • Best for: Top Savennières, Saumur Premier Cru, top Vouvray Sec
  • Key producers: Domaine du Closel, Château d'Epiré, Roches Neuves

🏺 Amphora / Concrete Egg

  • Properties: No flavor addition, allows micro-oxygen, natural convection
  • Effect: Combines pure minerality with rounded texture
  • Best for: New-generation natural wine production
  • Key producers: Vincent Carême, Domaine de la Sénéchalière

🌀 Lees Aging (Sur lie / Bâtonnage)

Many top Chenin dry whites undergo extended lees contact (6–18 months) with regular stirring (bâtonnage). This technique imparts additional roundness, nutty aromas, and more stable oxidative resistance — a common practice for Saumur Blanc and Savennières.
slides.4.quiz.question: Why do Chenin Blanc dry whites rarely use brand-new 225 L oak barrels?
slides.4.quiz.options.0: Chenin is not suitable for any oak contact
slides.4.quiz.options.1: Chenin's aromas are delicate; new barrel vanilla/cream notes easily overwhelm varietal character; Loire winemakers prefer large old barrels or neutral containers
slides.4.quiz.explanation: Chenin Blanc's aromatic profile (green apple, quince, white flowers, minerals) is very delicate, and the vanilla, butter, and toast notes from new barrels easily overshadow varietal and terroir character. This is why top Loire Chenin (Savennières, Saumur Blanc, Vouvray Sec) typically use 500–600 L Demi-Muid or neutral stainless/concrete. By contrast, Chardonnay (as in Burgundy) integrates new oak aromas more harmoniously.
slides.5.title: Level 3-1 Knowledge Test
slides.5.questions.0.question: What is the minimum Chenin Blanc percentage required in Anjou Blanc AOC?
slides.5.questions.0.explanation: Anjou Blanc requires ≥80% Chenin Blanc; up to 20% Sauvignon Blanc and/or Chardonnay may be blended. This flexibility allows estates to adjust their style — most top wines still choose 100% Chenin, while some add Sauvignon to boost aromatics. Saumur Blanc follows the same regulations.
slides.5.questions.1.question: Which sweetness levels are permitted in Savennières AOC?
slides.5.questions.1.explanation: Savennières is the only top Chenin Blanc AOC in Loire that mandates Sec only (dry; residual sugar <8 g/L). This strict rule forces estates to focus on the ultimate expression of Chenin dry wine, preventing residual sugar from masking terroir differences. Both independent Cru AOCs — Coulée de Serrant and La Roche-aux-Moines — follow the same rule.
slides.5.questions.2.question: Which biodynamic pioneer exclusively owns Coulée de Serrant?
slides.5.questions.2.explanation: Coulée de Serrant is an independent Cru AOC within Savennières, just 7 ha, a single vineyard since 1130 AD. Nicolas Joly converted it to biodynamic viticulture from the 1980s onward, becoming a global leader of the biodynamic wine movement. His book Wine from Sky to Earth is a classic in the field.
slides.5.questions.3.question: Why does Loire Chenin prefer large Demi-Muid barrels (500–600 L)?
slides.5.questions.3.options.1: Large barrels release oak flavor slowly, adding textural depth without masking Chenin's delicate varietal character
slides.5.questions.3.explanation: Demi-Muid (500 L) and Foudre (large vats) have a much lower ratio of wood surface area to wine volume than standard Barrique (225 L), so oak flavor is released more slowly and gently. This is especially important for the delicately aromatic Chenin Blanc — it gains the benefits of textural roundness and micro-oxygenation without being overwhelmed by new oak vanilla/butter notes.
